claims.text: Co-Mn-In is a transition-metal Heusler-type alloy system with magnetocaloric properties.
The undoped Co-Mn-In alloy has a broad transition-temperature range.
The undoped Co-Mn-In alloy has significant hysteresis.
Adding approximately 0.5 at.% Hf can fine-tune the behavior of the base alloy.
Approximately 0.5 at.% Hf will tune the magnetostructural transition of Co-Mn-In.
The beneficial magnetocaloric response will occur near room temperature under moderate magnetic fields.
Minor Hf addition will stabilize the Heusler-type phase.
Minor Hf addition will sharpen the magnetostructural transition.
Hf doping alters the local electronic environment.
Hf doping alters the local lattice environment.
The altered electronic and lattice environment produces a narrower and more abrupt phase transition.
A narrower and more abrupt transition increases the isothermal entropy change.
Hf doping reduces hysteresis energy losses during cyclic magnetic-field application.
The 0.5 at.% Hf alloy will have a larger adiabatic temperature change than the undoped alloy.
The 0.5 at.% Hf alloy will have lower magnetic hysteresis than the undoped alloy.
The beneficial effect exists only within a narrow Hf-concentration window.
Hf concentrations outside the beneficial window may cause phase instability or diminished magnetocaloric enhancement.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts that excessive Hf may cause phase instability or diminished enhancement, but the falsification rule also treats phase instability without enhancement at excessive Hf as sufficient to falsify the hypothesis. Thus an anticipated boundary behavior is incorrectly presented as a falsifier of the central 0.5 at.% Hf claim.
